newsitem.title: CHINA: China needs unified stock regulator - paper.
newsitem.headline: China needs unified stock regulator - paper.

text.p: China needs to unify the arms of its securities regulatory authorities to strengthen stock market supervision, the official Financial News said on Monday.
It also should abandon the quota system used to determine the pace of share offerings each year, the newspaper said.
China's stock regulatory system lacked real supervisory power because of separate organisations with conflicting roles, the newspaper said in a signed commentary.
The Securities Commission of the State Council (cabinet) acts as policy-maker while the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) implements policy and is responsible for supervision.
Provincial authorities have also set up their own regulatory bodies to oversee local market operations.
The commentary also called for a clearer definition of the regulator's supervisory powers although it gave no specific details of its view of possible reform.
China should move to allow listings based on the merits of each individual company seeking a listing, the commentary said.

China currently has an annual quota of shares that can be brought to market. In selecting firms to fill the quota it often considers the location of their operations to create a regional balance as well as the merits of the individual companies.
